gaps.sentence: There are ___ than forty applicants for every training place.
gaps.explanation: 'More than' + number expresses quantities above a figure.

gaps.sentence: It's so quiet here — there's hardly ___ around.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly' is a negative adverb, so it combines with 'anybody' (hardly anybody = almost nobody); 'nobody' would double the negative.

gaps.sentence: We had ___ luggage that the taxi couldn't take it all.
gaps.explanation: 'So much luggage that …' — luggage is uncountable.

gaps.sentence: Don't rush — we've got ___ of time.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ of time (no article needed)
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of time' needs no article; 'lot of time' would need 'a', and 'much of time' needs 'the'.

gaps.sentence: You can park on ___ side of the street.
gaps.hint: singular noun meaning 'this one or that one'
gaps.explanation: 'Either side' means one side or the other (both are allowed); 'both' would need the plural 'sides'.

gaps.sentence: One of my shoes is tighter than ___.
gaps.hint: shoes come in pairs of two
gaps.explanation: 'One ... than the other' is the pattern for two items; 'another' would suggest more than two.

gaps.sentence: There are too ___ tourists in Venice in August.
gaps.explanation: 'Too many' is used before countable plurals like tourists; 'too much' is for uncountables.

gaps.sentence: ___ of her two brothers lives abroad.
gaps.explanation: 'Each of her two brothers lives ...' is correct; 'every' cannot take 'of' and 'both/all' need a plural verb.
